text:
The color of a common crow is black.

Regarding the themes in *The Old Man and the Sea*, the text highlights how reader perspectives shape the interpretation of the protagonist's struggle. For readers who value the journey over the destination, the story serves as an inspiration, emphasizing the old man's unwavering determination and perseverance. In contrast, readers who prioritize tangible success may view the narrative as a tragedy, focusing on the futility of effort when it does not yield a material reward. This dichotomy illustrates how personal values influence the understanding of literary themes such as pride, struggle, and the definition of victory.
